The relative clause is אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.1.1 (tokens 5-6 of 16) and אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.2.1 (tokens 2-3 of 9); collated in both directions the run returns BYTE tier, so the seeing-verb is shared, not distinctive. The row's device_notes nevertheless read 'The header uses the seeing-verb chazah rather than the word-formula of the 2:1 header' - the 'rather than' sets the seeing-verb against the second header, which its own bytes carry. The intra-cluster contradiction is confirmed: the P01-008 device_notes say 'both retain the chazah seeing-verb and the ben-Amots patronymic', which the bytes support and which contradicts P01-001 as written. Row-internal checks that hold: oshb:Isa.1.1 is 16 tokens carrying a header noun, a relative clause and a four-king regnal list with no imperative, vocative or divine-speech frame, so the single-verse isolation ground stands; no parashah mark falls in the span and none is claimed; no ketiv/qere note falls in chapter 1 (verified against the 49-verse single-witness inventory); identity numbering, no offset zone touched, no dual owed. Staged book guidance calls the yod-initial byform unattested in Isaiah; the bytes of this verse contradict that. This is a staged-guidance erratum, NOT a row defect - the row makes no spelling claim - and it carries no remedy against the row.
P01-001.remedy: Field: P01-001 device_notes, first clause. Change: replace the 'seeing-verb chazah rather than the word-formula of the 2:1 header' contrast with a statement that both superscriptions carry the same relative clause (byte tier at oshb:Isa.1.1 and oshb:Isa.2.1) and that the header-noun class is the sole discriminator (חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙, byte tier). Test the cure must pass: a byte collate of the relative-clause run against oshb:Isa.2.1 returns byte tier - the test that killed the original - and the corrected sentence must read consistently with the P01-008 account of the same clause. P01-006.challenge_claim: The decision and every tier label verify exactly as written, but the one ground offered against the rival division - that the divine-speech signature at MT 1:24 is postpositive and not an onset - is contested by that form's byte position.

The campaign's tier-disclosure law makes form-class and position labels byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits, and 'postpositive ... not an onset frame in itself' is used here as a load-bearing ground for rejecting the 1:23|1:24 rival. On the bytes of this verse that ground does not hold, and it leans toward the rival that the tier-3 mark also points to. Upheld. Calibration - the row is otherwise exact and the cut is not defeated, which fixes severity at low. Independently confirmed: קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה at oshb:Isa.1.21 (tokens 4-5) and קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה at oshb:Isa.1.26 (tokens 12-13) collate at SKELETON tier in both directions and no higher, exactly matching the row's own skeleton-tier labelling and its two-verse digit; the woe lexeme at oshb:Isa.1.24 is genuinely non-initial (token 8) and governs first-person divine action, so the self-exclamation role reading holds; the PE at oshb:Isa.1.23 is correctly typed, never conflated with the chapter's SAMEKH sites, is the only marked verse inside 1:21-1:26, and is disclosed as the rival rather than buried, with confidence honestly reduced to medium_low. The challenge's 'available and unused' observation also verifies: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה at oshb:Isa.1.25 token 1 collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.1.26, whose token 1 is וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה - a byte-tier anaphora, but lying wholly on the far side of the rival cut, so it does not answer it. Not escalated: the strategy settles the precedence in play (a byte-grounded cohesion device outranks a tier-3 single-witness mark, and tier-3 never drives), and the residual 21-26 versus 21-23|24-26 question is a boundary matter the row already discloses and holds at reduced confidence - a proposal for boss adoption, not a peer policy escalation. P01-007.challenge_claim: The row asserts its opening seam carries no explicit lexical frame marker; in the bytes a two-term pair that co-occurs in only two verses of this chapter sits at exactly this row's opening verse and the preceding unit's opening verse. Second and smaller: the pointed splice for the closing verse stops short of the English paired with it.

Independently re-derived: the justice noun's substring sweep returns 40 verses; the justice/righteousness co-occurrence object returns 16 verses book-wide and exactly 2 inside chapter 1, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27 (sweep: 16 verses / 2 verses, skeleton) - the challenge's digits are exact. A frame marker in this book's spine is an onset device - imperative, vocative, messenger or speech formula, superscription, header. A thematic term-pair is a cohesion device, a different object. Verified: oshb:Isa.1.27 is 5 tokens, צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה, carrying no imperative, vocative or speech formula, so the row's assertion is byte-true as written and is not contradicted. Adjacent-verse root cohesion across a seam the row itself grades weakest is the disclosure that is owed; the 1:21/1:27 co-occurrence is a chapter-level bracket riding behind it. Severity stays medium: the row states that it has named its sole basis for this seam, and it has not. The second point is upheld exactly as written and is independent. Quote and gloss are not cut to the same extent, and campaign law repairs that by re-cutting the gloss. What holds: the discourse-mode shift is byte-carried, since oshb:Isa.1.25 and oshb:Isa.1.26 both open with the first-person cohortative וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה and oshb:Isa.1.27 does not; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.31 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse in the span. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.

P01-008.challenge_claim: The shared-feature claim across the two headers ships without tier labels, and its parts sit at three different tiers - one byte-identical, one accent-stripped-only, one skeleton-only.
P01-008.grounds: Every tier re-derives exactly as the challenge states, checked in the direction the row's own sentence asserts. P01-011.challenge_claim: One lens: the row treats 2:12 as a fresh unit onset without disclosing that it is grammatically continuative and lexically bonded to the refrain it treats as the prior unit's clean close. The other: the rejected alternative's load-bearing form label - an asyndetic catalogue - is contradicted by the pointed bytes, which show a waw-coordinated series.
P01-011.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT defects, not one defect seen twice: the first is an undisclosed cross-seam cohesion signal at the row's OPENING, the second a false form-class label inside the rejected alternative's INTERNAL-SPLIT argument. Neither subsumes the other; they sit in different fields and fail different tests. Form label, upheld and stronger than charged. Every member of the catalogue opens with the same conjunction-plus-preposition token: וְעַל֙ at oshb:Isa.2.13 token 1 and וְעַ֖ל at its token 7, and the same token at oshb:Isa.2.14 tokens 1 and 5, oshb:Isa.2.15 tokens 1 and 5, and oshb:Isa.2.16 tokens 1 and 5 - eight coordinated members, and the governing verse coordinates its own second phrase the same way (עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם at oshb:Isa.2.12 tokens 5-8 without the conjunction, וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל at tokens 9-12 with it). The series is polysyndetic, the exact opposite of the label, and the label is shipped TWICE - in strongest_rejected_alternative and again in device_notes. Form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits, so this is a defect even though the conclusion it supports (enumeration inside the governing oracle) survives correction. The accompanying charge that the row calls the quantifier a preposition is right but slight: the preposition is the head and the quantifier is its object, so the two-word phrase is not simply a preposition - a wording repair inside the same edit, not a third defect. Cross-seam cohesion, upheld. oshb:Isa.2.12 opens with כִּ֣י, the same particle that opens oshb:Isa.2.6 as כִּ֣י inside the preceding row's own span, and both witnesses render it subordinating there. The humbling/lofty root chain then runs unbroken across the seam: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל אִ֑ישׁ at oshb:Isa.2.9 tokens 1-4, שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.11 tokens 4-7, עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם and וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל at oshb:Isa.2.12, הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.13 tokens 5-6 and הָרָמִ֑ים / הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.2.14, closing again at oshb:Isa.2.17. Independently swept, the low/bow root alone stands at 10 verses book-wide and at exactly those four sites in this chapter (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton). That is adjacent-verse cohesion straddling this row's own opening seam, undisclosed, and it leaves the strongest rival - one sustained pride-and-humbling poem with the refrain as internal punctuation - unstated. Recorded but NOT counted as a defect: the flight-from-terror motif brackets this row with no member inside its span. A device lying wholly on both sides of a row argues at complex level only; it cannot argue continuity ACROSS either of this row's own seams, so it is a chapter-level note, not a cross-seam disclosure this row owes. What holds: the opening run is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.2.12 at byte tier; the closing refrain clause is verse-final and byte-identical to the earlier site (sweep: 2 verses, byte); no parashah mark falls inside 2:12-2:17 and the SAMEKH cited at the opening seam is correctly typed - mark handling is complete and honest. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 2. P01-011.remedy: Two fields, two independent edits. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes: replace the asyndetic label with the waw-coordinated (polysyndetic) description, and re-cut the quantifier wording so the preposition is named as head and the quantifier as its object; the internal-split rejection itself stands, since a coordinated series still hangs on the governing temporal clause. (2) device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure at the opening seam - the subordinating particle shared with oshb:Isa.2.6, and the humbling/lofty root chain running oshb:Isa.2.9, oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.12, oshb:Isa.2.13-14, oshb:Isa.2.17 (sweep: 10 verses book-wide, skeleton) - and state the sustained-poem rival it raises. Tests the cure must pass: the corrected form label must survive a token read of oshb:Isa.2.13 through oshb:Isa.2.16 showing the conjunction on every member - the test that killed the original; and the cohesion disclosure must be tier-labelled per site, since the chain is a root-level link, not a byte recurrence. P01-012.challenge_claim: The stated ground for this row's opening seam - a fresh topical turn to the idols at 2:18 - is contested by the bytes, since the idol lexeme is already in the preceding row at 2:8 and the flight-from-terror formula of 2:10 returns inside this row at 2:19 and 2:21.
P01-012.grounds: The digits verify and one of the two grounds does not survive re-derivation. Idol half, refuted on its own bytes. The lexeme stands at 8 verses book-wide and in this chapter at oshb:Isa.2.8, oshb:Isa.2.18 and oshb:Isa.2.20 (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton) - digits exact. But the challenge places the first site 'inside the preceding row', and it is not: אֱלִילִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.8 lies inside the 2:5-2:11 span, two rows upstream. The row immediately preceding this one is 2:12-2:17, and its bytes carry NO idol lexeme at any of its six verses. The row's own wording is scoped to exactly that adjacent unit - a fresh topical turn 'after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17' - and against the adjacent unit the turn genuinely is fresh. The resumption the challenge sees is real but operates at complex level, and the row already concedes complex-level continuity in device_notes by disclosing the temporal tag at oshb:Isa.2.20 (בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙). This ground does not stand. Flight half, upheld, and this is the row's real defect. Two members of the motif sit INSIDE this span - מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר at oshb:Isa.2.19 tokens 6-9 and the same four-token core at oshb:Isa.2.21 tokens 6-9 - while a third sits beyond the row's opening seam at oshb:Isa.2.10 (accent_stripped tier across the three on that object; the run collates none once the majesty noun is included, since the earlier site is defective). A device with a member inside the span and a member across the seam is adjacent-seam cohesion in the strict sense, and it is undisclosed. Second and separate: the eight-token run מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ is BYTE-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte), an in-span repetition of a strength the row never mentions while disclosing only the weaker temporal tag at its third verse. Corrected finding and severity: one stated ground is sound as scoped, the other is replaced by a genuine two-part disclosure gap that does not touch the bounds - so the grade drops from the charged level. What holds: the quoted opening run וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף is the entire verse at byte tier (oshb:Isa.2.18 is 3 tokens); the PE at oshb:Isa.2.22 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span; and the rejected alternative's negative claim is exact - the stanza-closing clause occurs at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.17, byte tier) and at neither end of this row. So the defect is engagement, not accuracy: a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carrying the weight of a not-cut decision ships with no pointed splice. What holds: כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.1 (byte tier); the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.3.12 is correctly typed and the only parashah mark inside 3:1-3:12; the PE cited at the opening seam is correctly typed; and neither of the chapter's two ketiv/qere verses falls inside this span, so nothing is owed there. The other: this row survives every check applied to it, but its superlative carries no digit and is scoped to a work partition rather than to the text.
P01-014.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT: different fields, different failure classes, and neither subsumes the other. Missing segmentation rival, upheld and the weightier of the two. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative argues trial_speech against judgment_oracle - an operative-category choice - and names no competing span at all. The identical disclosure already stands in device_notes as the mandated deviation note, so the field is duplicated onto a classification argument and the row ships with NO tested boundary rival: whether these three verses merge back into the leadership-collapse unit that precedes them, or run on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16, is never weighed. A mandated disclosure field carrying no instance of what it exists to disclose is a genuine defect, not a stylistic one. Undigited partition-scoped superlative, upheld. The boundary_rationale calls this the clearest contend-and-judge pairing 'in this part' - a superlative with no digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit, scoped to a workflow partition rather than to a verse range or to the book, and workflow references do not belong in row prose. Re-derived independently, the bytes license a stronger and fully checkable replacement: לָרִ֖יב at oshb:Isa.3.13 token 2 stands at 3 verses token-exact (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton - oshb:Isa.3.13, oshb:Isa.34.8, oshb:Isa.58.4) and לָדִ֥ין at token 5 at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton), so the pairing cannot recur anywhere else in the book - a book-scoped digit-bearing claim replacing a partition-scoped undigited one. Cross-row note: this partition-reference class recurs at P01-016, which brackets images over 'the part's own' range twice. It is a register sweep across the cluster, not two spot fixes. What holds, and it is most of the row: נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים is verse-initial and exhausts oshb:Isa.3.13 at byte tier (6 tokens); the closing signature נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת is verse-final at oshb:Isa.3.15 tokens 9-12 at byte tier with the exact title stack quoted rather than blended with the differently stacked signature earlier in the book; the ketiv/qere disclosure is exact and unusually careful - oshb:Isa.3.15 carries one note whose unpointed ketiv מלכם stands at token 1 with its pointed qere, eight tokens before the quoted signature, so the quoted run is genuinely unaffected exactly as the row says; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.3.15 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span, and the SAMEKH at the opening seam is correctly typed too. Identity numbering. Severity is set by the heavier item: an untested mandated rival outweighs a prose-and-digit repair.
P01-014.remedy: Two fields, one edit each. (2) P01-014 boundary_rationale: drop the workflow-partition scope and re-cut the superlative to a book-scoped digit-bearing claim (contend infinitive 3 verses, judge infinitive 1 verse, the pairing unique to this verse). Tests the cure must pass: the rewritten rival must name a competing SPAN and be disposed on the row's own bytes - a field that names no span fails the same test again; the re-cut superlative must carry a digit whose object is named and must contain no workflow reference; and the two disclosures must not restate one another, since duplication is what emptied the field. No boundary change is proposed - naming a rival is not adopting it.

P01-015.challenge_claim: The row's own grammatical label for the Isa.3.18-23 catalogue is imprecise - that verse opens with a single finite verb governing an accumulating list of accusative objects, not a construct/genitive chain as the row's prose labels it - though the underlying single-unit conclusion is sound.
P01-015.grounds: Re-derived from bytes and the label is a category error. oshb:Isa.3.18 is 9 tokens: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא at tokens 1-2 (the temporal formula), יָסִ֣יר at token 3 - a single finite verb - with its subject אֲדֹנָ֗י at token 4, the direct-object marker אֵ֣ת at token 5, and then the objects beginning תִּפְאֶ֧רֶת הָעֲכָסִ֛ים וְהַשְּׁבִיסִ֖ים וְהַשַּׂהֲרֹנִֽים. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative calls the catalogue 'grammatically one long construct chain governed by' the opening clause. A construct chain is a genitive nominal sequence; what governs here is a finite verb reaching its objects through the object marker. Individual items in the list are themselves construct phrases, which is the likely source of the slip, but the catalogue as a whole is an accusative object series, not one chain. Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits, so the label is a defect on its own terms. Severity low is right and the challenge says so itself: the conclusion the label supports - enumeration inside one governed clause rather than an independent list-register unit - is correct, and the owner-ruled list-register finding independently reaches the same result for this very catalogue. Correcting the label strengthens the argument rather than unsettling it, since a single finite verb reaching across six verses is a tighter grammatical bond than a construct chain would be.
